title: Many in Rome deny image-adoration and call the charge a Protestant calumny—so the true Roman doctrine must be sought
source_text: I. In Ecclesia Romana permulti, praecipue qui sunt de plebe cordatiores, & Doctores etiam nonnulli, queruntur se calumniam pati, quum dicuntur a Protestantibus imagines Dei Christique, & etiam sanctorum mortuorum adorare, ac profitentur non tantum se, sed Ecclesiam quoque suam ab hac adoratione esse alienissimam, nec eam cultum adorationis rei ulli omnino deferre, quam uni soli vero Deo. Igitur operae pretium duximus diligenter inquirere in veram Ecclesiae & Scholae Romanae doctrinam circa imaginum cultum & adorationem, tum ne quis ipsi sententiam alienam affingat, tum etiam ut pateat an merito Reformati calumniae accusentur, quum Ecclesiae Romanae adorationem imaginum tribuunt.
pass_a_gloss: In the Roman Church very many, especially the more thoughtful among the people, and even some Doctors, complain that they suffer calumny when Protestants say they adore images of God and Christ and also of dead saints, and they profess that not only they but their Church also is most alien from this adoration, and that it pays the cult of adoration to no thing at all except to the one only true God. Therefore we have judged it worthwhile carefully to inquire into the true doctrine of the Roman Church and School concerning the cult and adoration of images, both lest anyone fasten an alien opinion upon it, and also that it may appear whether the Reformed are justly accused of calumny when they attribute to the Roman Church the adoration of images.
pass_b_english: Many Romans—lay and some doctors—deny they adore images and call the charge a calumny.
They claim their Church gives adoration-cult only to the one true God.
So Le Blanc will dig out Rome’s real doctrine on image-cult, lest Reformers be falsely blamed for inventing it.

choices.why: Their profession of distance from image-adoration frames the inquiry.
